ⓐ.summary: Combustion occurs when oxygen in gaseous oxygen combines with a substance, while caloric escapes into the air, generating heat.

c1.text: ⓐ In combustion, oxygen in gaseous oxygen combines with the burning substance, and caloric escapes into the air, generating heat.

c2.text: Heat is a massless substance called caloric, and heat generation is the release of combined caloric.

c3.text: Gaseous oxygen is a compound of oxygen and caloric.

c4.text: Gases contain far more caloric than solids or liquids.

h1.text: When many solid substances combust, heat is generated and gas is produced at the same time.

h2.text: Since the produced gas requires large amounts of caloric, little or no caloric escapes, so heat should not be generated under ⓐ.

a.note: Solid-to-gas combustion consumes caloric rather than releasing it, attacking rather than strengthening ⓐ.

h3.text: Gunpowder containing oxygen compounds combusts explosively and releases massive heat without gaseous oxygen.

h4.text: Caloric in gaseous oxygen is not the source of heat generated during combustion.

b.note: Combustion releasing heat without gaseous oxygen undermines the claim that caloric from gaseous oxygen is the source of combustion heat.

h5.text: No matter how much heat released during combustion enters the air, the mass of air does not increase.

h6.text: If heat were a substance added to the air, air mass would increase.

c.note: The naive attack rc1 assumes caloric has mass, but since caloric is massless (c5), rc1 is undercut.
